informal: The Lean builds the time-labelled configuration graph of a clocked randomized machine and shows its transition matrix \(S\) is strictly forward and substochastic with bounded in-degree, and that \(p_0=e+Sp_0\in[0,1]^{V_0}\) has \(p_0(x_0)\) equal to the acceptance probability.

results.informal: For the configuration graph on \(V_0\) with coin-averaged matrix \(S\), reward \(e\) and start \(x_0\), \(S\) is strictly forward substochastic with bounded in-degree, \(p_0=e+Sp_0\) with \(p_0\in[0,1]^{V_0}\), and \(p_0(x_0)=p_{\mathcal M}(x)\).
results.note: These lemmas prove the three listed properties of the configuration reduction for the Lean graph, but the logarithmic-space computability of ports and weights is handled elsewhere and \(p_0\) is given as a bounded recursion rather than \((I-S)^{-1}e\).

decls.name: honestly
decls.informal: The data \((S,e,p_0)\) of the configuration graph form a correct hierarchy level: \(S\) is strictly forward and substochastic, \(e\ge0\), \(p_0\in[0,1]^{V_0}\) and \(p_0=e+Sp_0\).

chunks.ProbabilityDecision.honestly/0: Split correctness into four goals: the step conditions on \(S\), \(e\ge0\), \(p_0\in[0,1]\), and \(p_0=e+Sp_0\).
chunks.ProbabilityDecision.honestly/1: \(S\) is nonnegative, has entries \(\le1\), has row sums \(\le1\), and every positive entry \(S(i,j)\) has \(i,j\in V_0\) and \(i<j\).
chunks.ProbabilityDecision.honestly/1/0: Prove the step conditions on \(S\) one at a time.
chunks.ProbabilityDecision.honestly/1/2: \(S(i,j)\le 1\), which is the rate bound at level \(0\).
chunks.ProbabilityDecision.honestly/1/5: Then one of the two coin moves from \(i\) leads to \(j\).
chunks.ProbabilityDecision.honestly/1/6: A coin move from \(i\) to \(j\) gives \(i,j\in V_0\) and \(i<j\).
chunks.ProbabilityDecision.honestly/1/7: Apply this to whichever coin move leads to \(j\).
chunks.ProbabilityDecision.honestly/3/0: The bounded recursion for \(p_0\) stays in \([0,1]\).
chunks.ProbabilityDecision.honestly/5: \(p_0(i)\) equals \(e(i)\) plus the average of \(p_0\) over the two coin moves from \(i\).
chunks.ProbabilityDecision.honestly/6: The coin average equals \(\sum_{j\in V_0}S(i,j)p_0(j)\), so \(p_0(i)=e(i)+\sum_{j\in V_0}S(i,j)p_0(j)\).

decls.name: fair
decls.informal: Under the logarithmic space bound, \(p_0(x_0)\) equals the acceptance probability of \(\mathcal M\) on \(x\) within \(T(n)\) steps.

chunks.ConfigurationGraph.fair/0: Let \(k=T(n)\), let \(f_b(t)\) be the configuration at time \(t\) under coin string \(b\in\{0,1\}^k\), and let \(g_t(b)=p_0(f_b(t))\).
chunks.ConfigurationGraph.fair/1: For \(t<k\), \(g_t(b)=\tfrac12\bigl(g_{t+1}(b)+g_{t+1}(b')\bigr)\), where \(b'\) is \(b\) with bit \(t\) flipped.
chunks.ConfigurationGraph.fair/1/0: Let \(i=t\), let \(b'\) be \(b\) with bit \(i\) flipped, and extend coin strings to infinite coin tapes.
chunks.ConfigurationGraph.fair/1/1: \(f_b(t)=f_{b'}(t)\), since the first \(t\) coins of \(b\) and \(b'\) agree.
chunks.ConfigurationGraph.fair/1/1/0: It suffices that \(b\) and \(b'\) agree at every \(j<t\).
chunks.ConfigurationGraph.fair/1/1/3: So the positions \(i\) and \(j\) of the coin string differ.
chunks.ConfigurationGraph.fair/1/2: At time \(t<k\), the configuration under each of \(b,b'\) steps along its coin \(t\) to its time-\((t+1)\) configuration, and the configuration under \(b\) is not a final rewarded one.
chunks.ConfigurationGraph.fair/1/5: Using \(p_0=e+Sp_0\) at \(f_b(t)\) with \(e=0\) there, \(p_0(f_b(t))\) is the average of \(p_0\) over the two successors \(f_b(t+1)\) and \(f_{b'}(t+1)\).
chunks.ConfigurationGraph.fair/2: For every \(t\le k\), \(\sum_b g_0(b)=\sum_b g_t(b)\), by induction using the averaging identity and the fact that flipping bit \(t\) is a bijection.
chunks.ConfigurationGraph.fair/3: Let \(\mathrm{acc}(b)\) mean that \(\mathcal M\) outputs accept after \(k\) steps with coins \(b\).
chunks.ConfigurationGraph.fair/7: Thus \(2^k p_0(x_0)=\#\{b:\mathrm{acc}(b)\}\), which is \(2^k\) times the acceptance probability.

decls.name: in_degree
decls.informal: Each vertex \(y\) has at most \(|\mathcal H|\) predecessors \(i\) with \(S(i,y)>0\), where \(\mathcal H\) is a fixed finite set of hints depending only on the machine.

chunks.ConfigurationGraph.in_degree/0: Let \(v\) be the set of predecessors of \(y\) and, for each, let \(b_i\) be a coin that moves \(i\) to \(y\) (true if possible).
chunks.ConfigurationGraph.in_degree/1: Each \(i\in v\) moves to \(y\) with coin \(b_i\).
chunks.ConfigurationGraph.in_degree/1/0: \(i\in v\) means some coin moves \(i\) to \(y\).
chunks.ConfigurationGraph.in_degree/1/1: So the chosen coin \(b_i\) moves \(i\) to \(y\).
chunks.ConfigurationGraph.in_degree/2: Code each predecessor \(i\) by the hint of its configuration and coin \(b_i\) (old control and locally overwritten data).
chunks.ConfigurationGraph.in_degree/3: The hint code is injective on \(v\).
chunks.ConfigurationGraph.in_degree/3/1: The coin move from \(i\) lands at \(y\).
chunks.ConfigurationGraph.in_degree/3/2: The coin move from \(m\) lands at \(y\).
chunks.ConfigurationGraph.in_degree/3/3: Two configurations with the same successor and the same hint are equal.
chunks.ConfigurationGraph.in_degree/4: An injection from \(v\) into \(\mathcal H\) gives \(|v|\le|\mathcal H|\).
